original_card.question: What exact content and credit of a small named PR set has already been retained?
methods: Compare exact heads and retained artifacts to write a source-bound disposition receipt.
Audit an existing receipt for missing content or predecessor attribution.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Separate complete integration, partial retention and changed heads; make no autonomous closures.

first_step.inspect: Read one small PR set in the ledger and identify exact reviewed heads and unresolved content.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Compare that set to retained artifacts; produce a complete or explicitly partial disposition receipt.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Reliable overlap evidence preserves credit and prevents repeated review of already-retained material.
allowed_variations: One small related PR family or one existing integration receipt.
scope_change_triggers: Treating matching titles or one shared blob as proof of full incorporation.

actual_scope: What exact content and credit of a small named PR set has already been retained?
bottleneck_link: Reliable overlap evidence preserves credit and prevents repeated review of already-retained material: this receipt disposes of PR1's eleven paths and its credit row exactly, so no later session needs to re-authenticate them and no retained content stays uncredited.
stop_rule: If the PR1 head objects cannot be fetched and authenticated byte-exactly, or a shared-file hunk cannot be classified exactly, record the exact obstruction and report an explicitly partial receipt; never infer retention from matching titles or one shared blob.
evidence: research/pr1-retention-receipt/RESULT.json (exact per-path disposition of all 11 PR1 paths at head bfb168a5611c9eb219d04cf7d551edf1517ecd78 against base d8e0f83f00191df62174b641e9fff055c357f641, shared-file added-line survival counts, tree-mention inventory, and CONTRIBUTORS.md/ledger credit verification against live GitHub author metadata)
author: Aaron Wang
ai_assistance: with help from opencode (substantial AI assistance; no model named; no independent human review claimed)

open_questions.question: Are PR1's six distinctive artifacts (paired-tuned certificate, tuned-parameter doc, h50-paired-tuned patch and its three scripts/tests) needed by any retained downstream package under another name?
open_questions.why_it_matters: If a downstream package embeds their content without naming them, PR1's integration_location should record that package instead of staying empty.
open_questions.first_step: Hash each of the six files at PR1 head and search retained research trees for byte-identical or content-identical copies (done for exact bytes in this receipt; an adapted-content search needs a content-similarity index this package does not build).
open_questions.blocked_by: Adapted-content reuse is not detectable by exact hashing; a semantic reuse audit would need maintainer guidance on what counts as adoption.

open_questions.question: Does the fixed-exponent supremum claim in PR1's docs/paired-tuned-parameters.md survive the later two-stage topology and endpoint-copy work that CONTRIBUTORS.md says supersedes it?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The ledger keeps PR1 partially_reviewed; a scoped mathematical reassessment would decide whether the supremum argument adds anything to the current architecture.
open_questions.first_step: Read PR1's supremum proof against the later paid-endpoint construction it is said to feed (PR29 lineage) and state the precise surviving statement.
open_questions.blocked_by: That is a mathematical review task outside this source-retention receipt; the disposition here is source/credit only.
